Where it began

Shoaib Bashir was born in Chertsey on 13 October 2003 and grew up in Woking, going to Fullbrook School and Woking College. Before Somerset came calling he turned out for Guildford, for Berkshire in Minor Counties cricket and for Surrey and Middlesex age-group sides.

Somerset gave him a contract for 2023 after some sharp spells for their second team. He spent the winter before his first Somerset season playing club cricket in Australia with Lindfield. Both his first T20 Blast match and his first-class debut, against Essex, came in June 2023, and a month later he was part of the Somerset side that won the T20 Blast at Edgbaston.

The player

His rise was remarkable. A short clip of his first over in first-class cricket, bowling to Alastair Cook, was shared online and reached the England captain, Ben Stokes. By December 2023, with only six first-class matches behind him, he was in the Test squad for India. He made his Test debut at Visakhapatnam in February 2024, and later that month took 5 for 119, his first five-wicket haul in any first-class cricket.

The records kept coming. No England spinner had taken five wickets in a home Test at a younger age than he did against West Indies in July 2024. In May 2025, against Zimbabwe, he was the youngest Englishman to reach fifty Test wickets, taking six in the second innings and the match award. At Lord's in July 2025 he took the final wicket to win the Test against India. By November 2026 he had played 21 Tests and taken 71 wickets at 39.42, with four five-wicket hauls and a best of 6 for 81.

What made him special

He bowled right-arm off-spin, and youth was his calling card. Most of his records were about doing things sooner than anyone before him, and in India in 2024 only Paul Adams had taken a five-wicket haul there as a younger overseas spinner. For a tall man, he never felt the pull of seam bowling, which spinners everywhere will count as a win.

His batting was a gentler story. By November 2026 he had 106 Test runs, with a best of 14. But he had been not out in 18 of his 32 innings, which showed he was a hard man to get rid of, even if the runs were few.

Away from the middle

The Cricket Writers' Club named him its Young Player of the Year for 2024. In January 2026 he moved counties, signing a two-year contract with Derbyshire.

And finally

Plenty of young cricketers dream of a video of theirs catching the right person's eye. Bashir's did, and within months he was bowling in a Test match in India.
